title: Juniper and the Oath
premise: Jude Villalobos, a bone-carver who hears the dead through his carvings, keeps the ledgers of the Gilded Tooth, a guild that trades in impossible things. When the crown's witch-hunters arrive seeking anyone with the gift, Jude discovers the guild's founder made an oath to a buried king — an oath that has kept an ancient war frozen for three centuries, and that only a bone-speaker can renew or break. Hunted by Inquisitor Serane Voss and betrayed by the guildmaster who raised him, Jude must choose between renewing the oath (preserving a false peace built on the silenced dead) or breaking it and letting the war resume, while carrying the truth of what really started it. He breaks the oath, but not as anyone intended: he gives the dead king back his voice before the assembled courts, forcing a negotiated reckoning rather than a war, at the cost of his own hearing.
about_author: Rosalind Brightwater is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing guild records in coastal trading cities, where she developed a fascination with the paperwork of secrets. She writes fantasy about ordinary keepers of extraordinary obligations.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. We meet Jude carving a whalebone token that lets him hear a drowned sailor's last words, then filing it into the Gilded Tooth's ledgers. The guildmaster, Corvane, assigns him a routine appraisal. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking loneliness — Jude trusts no one with his gift, not even the man who found him.

chapters.title: Proclamation at the Salt Gate
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The crown posts a bounty on 'the hearing kind'; a neighbor is dragged away by Inquisitor Voss's hunters. Corvane burns a shelf of bone-tokens and tells Jude to hide his gift entirely. Emotional beat: fear curdling into anger as Jude realizes the ledgers he keeps are themselves evidence.

chapters.title: What the King's Rib Said
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Appraising a smuggled reliquary, Jude touches a rib-bone and hears a king's voice mid-oath: 'until one of the hearing kind speaks my name freely.' He realizes the guild's founding charter is a binding instrument. Emotional beat: vertigo — his whole life sits atop a buried mechanism.

chapters.title: Voss Comes to the Gilded Tooth
chapters.summary: Alternating Jude and Voss POV. Voss inspects the guild under pretext of tax audit; Jude lies for the first time in his life and nearly fails. Voss leaves unconvinced, taking a junior carver for questioning. Emotional beat: guilt — Jude survives because someone else pays.

chapters.title: Corvane's Confession
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Confronted, Corvane admits he bought Jude as a child precisely because the oath requires a bone-speaker to maintain it; Jude was never family, only a tool being fattened for use. Emotional beat: betrayal reframing every kindness Jude remembers.

chapters.title: The Drowned Choir
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, fleeing to the harbor slums. Among outcast hearers hiding beneath the tide-flats, Jude learns the war didn't start with the dead king's death but with the living courts' perjury — the secret that could reignite or end everything. Emotional beat: belonging found among the hunted.

chapters.title: A Price in Bone
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss captures the drowned choir; offered promotion if she delivers a bone-speaker alive, she begins doubting the hunt's true purpose when she reads sealed orders. Emotional beat: her certainty cracking — the hunter realizing she serves the lie.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Oath
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. To save the choir, Jude trades himself to Corvane, who needs him to renew the oath before the solstice. At the crypt, instead of renewing it, Jude carves the king's name and speaks it freely — the oath shatters. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into resolve.

chapters.title: The King Speaks
chapters.summary: Alternating Jude and Voss POV. Climax: with the war unfreezing, Jude uses the last of his fading gift to make the dead king testify before both courts, exposing the original perjury. Voss turns her hunters against the crown's faction. Emotional beat: terrible, costly vindication.

chapters.title: Silence, and What Remains
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, epilogue-like. The gift is gone; the dead are quiet at last. Jude rebuilds the guild as a school where hearers and non-hearers learn the true history, and Voss becomes its reluctant first patron. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted — justice outside the law, paid for in silence.
